Polymorphism

Stage 5 Concept ⏱ 15 min 📖 Glossary

One remote, many TVs: a common type (Animal) controls different objects (Dog, Cat) — each responds its own way.

🔎 Motivating questionHow does one “play” button work for songs, videos, and podcasts?

Objectives

  • Use parent type for children
  • Trace which method runs
  • Explain why it is useful

Needs first: Method Overriding

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

Universal remote: button speak() on slot Animal. Insert Dog cartridge → Woof; Cat → Meow. Remote never changes; cartridges vary.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: remote only has shared buttons. Dog-only trick fetch() needs a Dog remote (cast) — not on Animal.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

Animal a = new Dog(); Reference = general, object = specific. Call shared methods; JVM picks the real one.

Enables lists of mixed animals, plug-in behavior, test doubles.

Needs inheritance/interface + override. Compile checks Animal; run uses Dog.

3 Watch it move: Remote

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
class Animal { void speak(){ System.out.println("..."); } }
class Dog extends Animal {
  @Override void speak(){ System.out.println("Woof!"); }
}
class Cat extends Animal {
  @Override void speak(){ System.out.println("Meow!"); }
}
Animal[] zoo = { new Dog(), new Cat() };
for (Animal a : zoo) a.speak();
▶ Output Woof! Meow!
  • One array, two species.
  • Same call, two sounds.
  • New animal? Just add cartridge.
💡 Why this output?Each object’s override runs — one loop, many behaviors.

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: a.fetch() on Animal refWhy: Button missing on remote.
✅ Fix: Add to Animal or cast to Dog.
❌ Mistake 2: “Which runs? Reference type.”Why: Object type wins!
✅ Fix: new Dog() → Dog.speak.
❌ Mistake 3: If-else per type everywhereWhy: Defeats the point.
✅ Fix: Rely on override.
